text: PlugBox 是面向 DeepSeek Harness 网页端的插件中心，在 DSH 侧栏提供统一的插件管理面板。它通过侧栏入口打开同源页面，并调用宿主的 pluginManager 与 pluginMarket 服务。用户可以浏览和搜索插件索引、安装插件包、查看已安装插件、启用或停用插件，并移除插件或管理索引源。适合希望在 DSH 中集中发现和维护插件的用户。插件索引及仓库分支信息从 GitHub 获取；代码中未发现必需的 API 密钥配置。

PlugBox adds a plugin center to the DSH web sidebar. It uses host plugin services to search indexes, install bundles, view installed plugins, toggle them, remove them, and manage index sources. Index and branch data come from GitHub; the code shows no required API key.
想在 DSH 里集中搜索和安装插件。

I want one panel to browse plugin indexes and manage installed bundles.
PlugBox 的功能「插件浏览与管理」：侧栏插件中心连接 DSH 的插件市场和管理服务。打开面板后可浏览、搜索索引条目，安装插件包，并查看、启用、停用或移除已安装插件。
PlugBox 使用前须知：索引与分支信息从 GitHub 获取；代码未见必需 API 密钥。（见 index.js:176-212、index.js:227-237）

plugbox README · PlugBox：插件适配与管理工具：**中文** | [English](README.en.md)

**PlugBox 是一个插件适配与管理工具**：面向所有支持自定义插件的引擎层与智能体层工具，在同一套界面里浏览、安装、更新、启用或停用插件。它不再绑定任何单一引擎——宿主之间的差异全部封装在适配器里，核心层只回答「插件是什么」。

它目前以 DeepSeek Harness 插件（组合包）的形式分发，并对外发布一份可被任意 DSH 实例订阅的插件索引。

plugbox README · PlugBox：插件适配与管理工具：最短安装路径：在 DeepSeek Harness 的「发现 → Index sources」里加上 `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Wcof/PlugBox/main/index.json`，搜索 `plugbox` 安装，重启窗口；或在命令行执行 `dsh plugin --profile web add github:Wcof/PlugBox`。

如果你在找「某某引擎的插件在哪里装」「有没有一个能统一管理插件的市场」，这个项目提供的就是那层界面。插件列表来自宿主真实的 `pluginManager` / `pluginMarket` 服务，不维护第二份数据。

---

plugbox README · 为什么分层：插件生态的真正差异不在「装不装得上」，而在每个宿主怎么描述自己：清单字段叫什么、插件怎么注册 UI、RPC 方法叫什么名字、插件交付的能力落成什么结构。把这些塞进一套逻辑里，接第二个宿主时就会到处是 `if`。

PlugBox 因此分成两层：

plugbox README · 核心层 `src/core/`（与任何引擎无关）：| 位置 | 职责 |
|---|---|
| `protocol/plugin.ts` | 宿主无关的插件协议：`CanonicalPlugin`、`PluginVersion`、`Requirements`、`ResourceKind`、`PluginResource`、`Provenance` |
| `protocol/catalog.ts` | 索引条目结构与出处判定；标记的名字由适配器声明，核心只负责按规则算 |
| `protocol/version.ts` | 版本比较 |
| `protocol/brand.ts` | 产品自身的身份常量（品牌名、包名、标记词、索引文件名） |
| `manifest/index.ts` | 清单双向转换：`readManifest` / `toCanonical` / `writeManifest` / `toInstallSpec` |
| `resources/index.ts` | 插件资源（模型 / 工具 / 配置 / 文件 / UI 槽位）的统一抽象 |
section: 核心层 `src/core/`（与任何引擎无关）

text: plugbox README · 核心层 `src/core/`（与任何引擎无关）：核心刻意不认识任何具体宿主的字段名。兼容要求一律写成带命名空间的 `requirements['<宿主id>/<要求名>']`，例如 `'dsh/dsh'`；资源最终落到宿主的哪个位置由适配器决定。

`src/adapters/types.ts` 定义 `HostAdapter` 契约，一个适配器要交代：
section: 适配层 `src/adapters/`（每个目标宿主一个适配器）

text:
plugbox README · 适配层 `src/adapters/`（每个目标宿主一个适配器）：| 契约 | 内容 |
|---|---|
| `ui` | 挂载前缀、RPC 路径、模块 id、locale 命名空间、占用的 UI 槽位 |
| `labels` | 来源标签三档的展示名（官方那一档写宿主自己的名字，从适配器取） |
| `catalog` | 索引格式、出处判定策略、本产品在该宿主索引里的来源标记词 |

| `resources` | canonical 资源 → 宿主申领；返回 `null` 表示该宿主接不住这类资源 |
| `methods` | canonical 动词 → 宿主真实调用名 |
| `installSpec` | canonical 描述 → 宿主安装参数 |

text: plugbox README · 插件管理：顶部是来源统计卡，点卡片即筛选。每张卡片显示标题、包名、来源、运行状态和插件行数；点「详情」进入逐行启停页。

plugbox README · 插件市场：按索引源分组显示条目，卡片上标来源、状态（可安装 / 已安装 / 可更新 / 版本不符）和当前版本。工具栏支持搜索、来源 chips、创作者多选和多种排序；索引超过 100 条时按 `nextOffset` 续页，超上限会在列表上方如实提示「索引共 N 个，已加载 M 个」。

来源标签由当前适配器提供（见下表），因此不同宿主下「官方」那一档显示的文字不同——在 DSH 里显示为「DSH 官方」。

plugbox README · 按分支安装：点卡片左下角的版本号，弹出该仓库的分支列表：

- 每个分支显示名称、包内版本号、该宿主要求的兼容范围，以及分支自己的标题与描述（不同分支的描述可能不一样）；
- 没声明对应宿主插件字段的分支（在 DSH 上是 `dsh.bundle`）禁用安装；
- 已装的版本会标「当前已装」，此时换分支需要先卸载。

装的是**分支当前的头提交**：上游后续推送会改变它。要固定版本，还是等上游发 tag 后走正常安装。

分支列表由 Host 半边用 `git ls-remote --heads` 读取（不消耗 GitHub API 配额），失败才退回 GitHub REST。

plugbox README · 检查更新：页面打开时会静默比对索引与已装版本，有可更新就在顶部提示；点「检查更新」可强制刷新索引缓存。

plugbox README · 来源标签：三种标签含义不同：

| 标签 | 含义 | 判定方式 |
|---|---|---|
| **宿主官方** | 当前宿主官方维护或官方收录。展示名由适配器提供（DSH 下为「DSH 官方」） | 适配器声明的 `vendorLabels` 命中（DSH 为条目 `metadata.labels` 含 `official`） |
| **PlugBox 收录** | 收录在本仓库维护的索引里 | 索引条目 `metadata.keywords` 含 `plugbox` |
| **第三方** | 来自其他订阅的索引源 | 以上都不满足 |

判定函数 `provenanceOf(entry, policy)` 在核心层，规则 `ProvenancePolicy` 由适配器声明——核心不认识任何宿主的字段名，所以新增一个「官方用 `keywords.vendor` 表示」的宿主时，只加适配器即可。

plugbox README · 来源标签：**「PlugBox 收录」是本站的整理，不代表任何宿主官方背书。** 收录标准：仓库真实存在、确为目标宿主的插件（在 DSH 上表现为声明 `dsh.bundle`、可被 `dsh plugin add` 安装）、版本与许可证可核对（仓库 `package.json` / `LICENSE`）、插件版本已发布或至少对应一个确定的提交。当前收录 10 个插件，覆盖阅读、学习、效率、界面增强、工具、模型六个分类。

想推荐插件：在本仓库开 issue，附仓库地址、目标版本号与许可证；核对通过后由维护者加入收录库。

---

plugbox README · 精选索引 `index.json`：人工精选的收录库，随仓库发布，格式为 DSH 插件索引 `format: 1`，可被任何 DSH 实例订阅。三个入口：

| 入口 | 地址 | 说明 |
|---|---|---|
| GitHub Raw | `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Wcof/PlugBox/main/index.json` | 始终最新，推荐 |
| jsDelivr | `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/Wcof/PlugBox@main/index.json` | CDN 镜像，缓存约 12 小时 |
| 仓库内文件 | 仓库根目录下的 `index.json` | 随仓库一起签出，构建时生成 |

索引由 `src/data/catalog.ts`（收录库）+ `src/data/pluginIndex.ts`（生成器）产出，`npm run build` 后同步到根目录 `index.json`，并用 DSH 生态的官方校验器 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-plugin-market-index` 验证。

plugbox README · 精选索引 `index.json`：每个版本的 `source` 为 `{ type: "git", url, commit }`；`engines.dsh` 原样镜像该提交的 `package.json`——索引里省略表示「任意 DSH 版本」，所以不能想当然地留空。

jsDelivr 长时间不更新时手动刷新：

```bash
curl https://purge.jsdelivr.net/gh/Wcof/PlugBox@main/index.json
```

plugbox README · 社区目录 `community.json`：精选索引只有十几条，翻不到想要的那个。仓库因此另外发布一份**社区目录**：从第三方站点 [dsh-plugin.org](https://dsh-plugin.org) 同步的社区插件，逐条做过仓库级核实——仓库可达、该提交的 `package.json` 声明了宿主要求的插件字段、版本号取自包本身。条目统一带 `community` 标记词，用于和精选条目区分。

- `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Wcof/PlugBox/main/community.json`

订阅方式二选一：在 DSH「发现 → Index sources」里加上面这条地址；或在面板的工具栏点「社区目录」一键订阅。条目较多（数千条），搜索比逐页翻更高效；列表按批渲染，点「显示更多」继续加载。

社区目录里的条目只代表「这个仓库确实是一个目标宿主的插件包」，不代表我们验证过它的行为或兼容性；能否安装仍以宿主按 `engines.dsh` 的判断为准。

---

plugbox README · 给插件作者：清单与资源映射：核心层做清单转换时**刻意经过一层「中间视图」**：宿主的插件资格字段（例如 DSH 要求 `package.json` 里声明 `dsh.bundle.patch`）是宿主专属的，直接塞进 canonical 会把核心污染回去；完全丢掉又会让插件在目标宿主上装不起来。

```
宿主 package.json ──adapter.manifest.extract──▶ 中间视图 ManifestView（宿主专属字段原样保留在 hostFields）
中间视图 ──toCanonical──▶ CanonicalPlugin（纯中立描述）
CanonicalPlugin + 资源 ──writeManifest──▶ 目标宿主的 package.json 片段
```

对插件作者来说，只有三件事值得注意：
section: 给插件作者：清单与资源映射

text:
plugbox README · 给插件作者：清单与资源映射：1. **兼容范围写成区间，不要枚举预发布版本。** `>=0.2.1-rc.2 <0.3.0-0` 一次覆盖整个 0.2.1 系列，不用每个 rc 都改；写成 `0.2.1-rc.2 || 0.2.1-rc.3` 会在下一个 rc 发布当天失效。完整排查见 [docs/article-engine-incompatible.md](docs/article-engine-incompatible.md)。
2. **兼容字段是宿主的，键会被加命名空间。** 核心统一存 `requirements['<宿主id>/<要求名>']`，由 `requirementKeyOf` 映射（DSH 的 `engines.dsh` → `dsh/dsh`），写回时再剥掉。别在核心层期待看到原始字段名。
3. **资源按种类声明。** 统一的资源种类为 `command` / `tool` / `skill` / `model` / `prompt` / `config` / `file` / `ui-slot` / `transport`。同一份资源在不同宿主里落成不同结构（UI 槽位在 DSH 里是 `sidebar.panellist` + `main`），这份差异由 `HostAdapter.resources.map` 负责；接不住的资源会返回 `null` 而不是假装兼容。
section: 给插件作者：清单与资源映射

text:
plugbox README · 兼容性与边界：- 验收环境：DeepSeek Harness `0.2.1-rc.5`（npm `latest`）。宿主升级后建议重跑 `npm run check:engines` 核对索引。
- 兼容判定在宿主侧：`engines.dsh` 存在时只按它判断（忽略 peerDependencies），规则是 `semver.satisfies(运行时版本, range, { includePrerelease: true })`。这条规则属于 DSH 生态，由 DSH 适配器的 `satisfies` 实现；适配器不实现时核心只返回 `unknown`，不猜。
- 分支安装只展示分支声明的兼容范围，面板无法预判是否兼容（运行时版本没有暴露给页面），真正的判定发生在安装时。
- 索引每个插件只登记一个已发布版本；要装其他版本走分支安装，或等索引升版。
- 不提供插件配置界面：DSH 的远程面只暴露组合包与插件行的启停、安装、卸载，配置 schema 在模型侧（`Config.listConfigs`）。
- 未实测的适配器不会被选为默认宿主适配器。

---

plugbox README · 常见问题：**PlugBox 和宿主自带的「发现」页有什么区别？**
两者读同一套宿主服务。自带的「发现」页一次浏览一个索引；PlugBox 聚合多个索引源，额外提供作者分面、兼容性标记与按分支安装。

**PlugBox 支持哪些宿主？**
见上方支持矩阵。目前只有 DeepSeek Harness 在真实宿主上跑通过；zcode 的 DeepSeek Harness 是已知宿主但尚未实测。新增一个宿主 = 新增一个适配器 + 少量配置，不需要改核心。

**「PlugBox 收录」是宿主官方收录吗？**
不是。它只表示该插件被本仓库维护的索引收录。宿主官方收录按各宿主自己的标记判定（DSH 是条目 `labels` 里的 `official`），两者在界面上用不同标签区分。

plugbox README · 常见问题：**为什么某个插件显示「版本不符」？**
该版本声明的兼容范围（`engines.dsh`）不包含你当前的 DSH 版本。卡片上会写出它要求的范围，升级 DSH 或等插件放宽声明后才能装。完整排查见 [docs/article-engine-incompatible.md](docs/article-engine-incompatible.md)。

**按分支安装和正常安装有什么不同？**
正常安装装的是索引登记的固定提交；分支安装装的是分支当前的头提交，会随上游推送变化，适合上游还没发版的修复。

**为什么装完要重启？**
插件的 Host 端代码在 DSH 启动时加载，前端资源可以热更，Host 代码不能。

**索引源加了但看不到插件？**
先确认 URL 可访问（浏览器打开应返回 JSON），再在面板点「检查更新」刷新缓存；jsDelivr 有约 12 小时缓存，必要时用上面的 purge 命令。

plugbox README · 常见问题：**旧的 DeepSeekBox 订阅地址还能用吗？**
不能。仓库已改名为 **Wcof/PlugBox**，旧的 `Wcof/DeepSeekBox` 索引地址已失效。请在「Index sources」里删除旧地址，改订阅 `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Wcof/PlugBox/main/index.json`（或对应的 jsDelivr 地址）；已安装的旧版本可以用方式二重新从新地址安装覆盖。

npm install
npm run dev              # 开发服务器 http://localhost:5180，自带假宿主 mock
npm run build            # 类型检查 + 构建到 web/，自动跑 postbuild（索引同步与各项校验）

client.js             Client 半边：侧栏入口 + 主面板 iframe

text:
plugbox README · PlugBox: plugin adapter and management tool：If you are looking for "where do I install plugins for engine X" or "is there one marketplace to manage them all", this is that layer. The plugin list comes from the host's real `pluginManager` / `pluginMarket` services — there is no second copy of the data.

---
section: PlugBox: plugin adapter and management tool

text:
plugbox README · Why it is layered：The real difference between plugin ecosystems is not whether a plugin installs, but how each host describes itself: what its manifest fields are called, how a plugin registers UI, what its RPC methods are named, and which structure a plugin's capabilities collapse into. Put that in one codebase and the second host turns into `if` statements everywhere.

PlugBox is therefore split in two.

plugbox README · Core layer `src/core/` (host-agnostic)：One plugin protocol, manifest parsing and generation, registration and discovery, lifecycle management, and the abstraction for plugin resources.

plugbox README · Core layer `src/core/` (host-agnostic)：| Location | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `protocol/plugin.ts` | The host-neutral plugin protocol: `CanonicalPlugin`, `PluginVersion`, `Requirements`, `ResourceKind`, `PluginResource`, `Provenance` |
| `protocol/catalog.ts` | Catalog entry shape and provenance rules; markers are declared by adapters, the core only evaluates them |
| `protocol/version.ts` | Version comparison |
| `protocol/brand.ts` | The product's own identity constants (brand name, package name, markers, index file names) |
| `manifest/index.ts` | Two-way manifest conversion: `readManifest` / `toCanonical` / `writeManifest` / `toInstallSpec` |
| `resources/index.ts` | Unified abstraction for plugin resources (models / tools / config / files / UI slots) |

plugbox README · Core layer `src/core/` (host-agnostic)：The core deliberately does not know any host's field names. Requirements are always namespaced as `requirements['<host-id>/<requirement-name>']`, e.g. `'dsh/dsh'`, and where a resource lands in the host is decided by the adapter.

plugbox README · Adapter layer `src/adapters/` (one adapter per target host)：In one sentence: **the adapter answers "how does this host talk"; the core answers "what is a plugin".**

`src/adapters/types.ts` defines the `HostAdapter` contract. Each adapter declares:
section: Adapter layer `src/adapters/` (one adapter per target host)

text:
plugbox README · Adapter layer `src/adapters/` (one adapter per target host)：| Contract | Contents |
|---|---|
| `ui` | Mount prefix, RPC path, module id, locale namespace, claimed UI slots |
| `labels` | Display names for the three provenance badges (the vendor tier uses the host's own name, read from the adapter) |
| `catalog` | Index format, provenance policy, and the marker word this product uses in that host's index |
| `manifest` | Two-way conversion (`extract` / `compose` / `requirementKeyOf`), plus the optional `satisfies` range check and `pluginGate` admission check |
| `resources` | Canonical resource → host claim; returning `null` means this host cannot carry that kind of resource |
| `methods` | Canonical verb → the host's real call name |
| `installSpec` | Canonical description → host install argument |
section: Adapter layer `src/adapters/` (one adapter per target host)

text: plugbox README · Adapter layer `src/adapters/` (one adapter per target host)：**Adding a host means adding one directory that implements `HostAdapter` plus registering it — the core does not change.** Conversely, if a new host forces you to edit `src/core/`, the design is wrong.
section: Adapter layer `src/adapters/` (one adapter per target host)

text:
plugbox README · Host-specific terms: kept, and attributed：The following are **DeepSeek Harness's own protocol fields, file formats and commands**, supplied by the DSH adapter. They are what makes a plugin actually installable in DSH — **they are not product copy and must not be "neutralised"**:

`dsh.bundle` (bundle declaration) · `engines.dsh` (compatibility range) · `cordis.patch.yml` (bundle patch) · `dsh plugin add` (install command) · `pluginManager` / `pluginMarket` (host services)

plugbox README · Host-specific terms: kept, and attributed：The full contract lives in [docs/hosts/dsh-spec.md](docs/hosts/dsh-spec.md). It belongs to the DSH adapter, **not to the core**: another host means another contract document.

---

plugbox README · Support matrix：| Host | Adapter id | Host protocol / commands | Verified | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DeepSeek Harness (DSH) | `dsh` | `dsh.bundle` · `cordis.patch.yml` · `engines.dsh` · `dsh plugin add` | **Yes** (`0.2.1-rc.5`) | The first supported host and the only adapter currently exercised on a real host; contract in [docs/hosts/dsh-spec.md](docs/hosts/dsh-spec.md) |
| DeepSeek Harness by zcode | `zcode-dsh` | Same protocol family as DSH | **No** | Known host, not yet verified on a real environment. Differences in CLI entry point, profile layout and UI slots are still to be filled in; until then it must not be advertised as supported |

plugbox README · Support matrix：> Any host missing from this table is not integrated. **DSM Harness excluded: there is no adapter for it, and its existence must not be read as coverage.**
> Unverified adapters carry `verified: false` in the contract and are never selected by default; adapters with open questions also carry `openQuestions`.

plugbox README · Install：PlugBox currently ships as a DeepSeek Harness bundle — `dsh.bundle.patch` in `package.json` is a DSH protocol field supplied by the DSH adapter. Pick one of three ways; on another host the install argument comes from that host's `HostAdapter.installSpec`.

plugbox README · 1. From the plugin index (recommended)：1. Open the DeepSeek Harness **Discover** page and add this URL under *Index sources*:
   `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Wcof/PlugBox/main/index.json`
2. Search for `plugbox`, then install.
3. Restart the DSH window — host-side code is loaded at startup.

plugbox README · 2. From GitHub：In the panel's **Install plugin** dialog, enter either:

- `github:Wcof/PlugBox`
- `git+https://github.com/Wcof/PlugBox#<commit-sha>` (pinned to a commit, useful for reproducing issues)

Or from the DSH CLI (`--profile` takes your profile name; desktop is usually `desktop`):

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add github:Wcof/PlugBox
```

plugbox README · 3. From a local directory (development)：Enter the absolute path of this repository in the same dialog, e.g. `/Users/you/code/PlugBox`. Run `npm run build` and commit `web/` after frontend changes — git installs do not run a build.

---

plugbox README · Plugin management：The top row shows origin counters; clicking a card filters the list. Each card shows title, package name, origin, runtime status and plugin-row count. **Details** opens the per-row enablement page.

plugbox README · Plugin market：Entries are grouped by index source. Cards show provenance, status (installable, installed, update available, version mismatch) and the current version. The toolbar offers search, source chips, multi-select author facets and sort orders. Indexes longer than 100 entries are paged by `nextOffset`; when the page cap is hit, the list says so instead of silently truncating.
plugbox README · Plugin market：Provenance badges come from the active adapter (see below), so the *official* tier is worded per host — under DSH it reads "DSH official".

plugbox README · Install from a branch：You are installing **the branch's current head commit**, which upstream can move at any time. For a fixed version, wait for a tagged release and use the normal install path.

The branch list is read by the host half with `git ls-remote --heads` (no GitHub API quota), falling back to the GitHub REST API only when git is unavailable.

plugbox README · Update checks：The panel silently compares installed versions with the index on open and shows a banner when updates exist. **Check for updates** forces an index refresh.

---

plugbox README · Provenance labels：| Badge | Meaning | How it is decided |
|---|---|---|
| **Host official** | Maintained or curated by the current host's vendor. The display name comes from the adapter (under DSH: "DSH official") | The adapter's declared `vendorLabels` match (for DSH: `official` in the entry's `metadata.labels`) |
| **PlugBox catalog** | Listed in this repository's index | Index entry has `plugbox` in `metadata.keywords` |
| **Third-party** | Comes from another subscribed index | Neither of the above |

plugbox README · Provenance labels：`provenanceOf(entry, policy)` lives in the core while the `ProvenancePolicy` markers come from the adapter, so the core never learns a host's field names — adding a host that marks officials with `keywords.vendor` is an adapter-only change.

plugbox README · Provenance labels：**"PlugBox catalog" is this project's curation, not an endorsement by any host vendor.** Inclusion criteria: the repository exists, it really is a plugin for the target host (under DSH: declares `dsh.bundle` and installs with `dsh plugin add`), version and license are verifiable from `package.json` / `LICENSE`, and the version corresponds to a release or a fixed commit. The index currently lists 10 plugins across six categories: reading, learning, productivity, UI, tools, models.

plugbox README · Provenance labels：To suggest a plugin, open an issue with the repository URL, target version and license.

---

plugbox README · The curated index `index.json`：A hand-picked catalog published with the repository in DSH's `format: 1`, subscribable by any DSH instance. Three entry points:

| Entry point | URL | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| GitHub Raw | `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Wcof/PlugBox/main/index.json` | Always current, recommended |
| jsDelivr | `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/Wcof/PlugBox@main/index.json` | CDN mirror, ~12 h cache |
| In-repository file | `index.json` at the repository root | Checked out with the repo, generated on build |

plugbox README · The curated index `index.json`：The index is generated from `src/data/catalog.ts` (the catalog) by `src/data/pluginIndex.ts` (the builder); `npm run build` writes the root `index.json` and validates it with the DSH ecosystem's official validator `@deepseek-ai/dsh-plugin-market-index`.

Every version carries `source: { type: "git", url, commit }`, and `engines.dsh` mirrors the `package.json` at that commit — leaving the field empty means "any DSH version", so it must not be filled in casually.

If jsDelivr lags, purge it:

plugbox README · The curated index `index.json`：```bash
curl https://purge.jsdelivr.net/gh/Wcof/PlugBox@main/index.json
```

plugbox README · The community catalog `community.json`：The curated index only carries a dozen entries. The repository also publishes a **community catalog** synced from the third-party site [dsh-plugin.org](https://dsh-plugin.org), where every entry was verified at repository level: the repo is reachable, its `package.json` at that commit declares the plugin field the host requires, and the version comes from the package itself. Entries carry a `community` marker so they can be told apart from curated ones.

plugbox README · The community catalog `community.json`：- `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Wcof/PlugBox/main/community.json`

Subscribe from DSH's Discover → Index sources, or click **Community catalog** in the panel's market toolbar. With thousands of entries, search beats paging; the list renders in batches with a **Show more** button.

Being listed there means "this repository really is a plugin package for the target host" — not that its behaviour or compatibility was tested. The host still decides installability by `engines.dsh`.

---

plugbox README · For plugin authors: manifests and resource mapping：The core converts manifests **through an intermediate view on purpose**: a host's plugin-eligibility field (DSH requires `dsh.bundle.patch` in `package.json`) is host-specific — pushing it into the canonical shape would pollute the core back, and dropping it entirely would make the plugin uninstallable on the target host.
section: For plugin authors: manifests and resource mapping

text:
plugbox README · For plugin authors: manifests and resource mapping：```
host package.json ──adapter.manifest.extract──▶ intermediate ManifestView (host fields preserved verbatim in hostFields)
intermediate view ──toCanonical──▶ CanonicalPlugin (purely neutral description)
CanonicalPlugin + resources ──writeManifest──▶ target host's package.json fragment
```

Only three things matter if you author plugins:
section: For plugin authors: manifests and resource mapping

text:
plugbox README · For plugin authors: manifests and resource mapping：1. **Write compatibility as a range, not as an enumeration of prereleases.** `>=0.2.1-rc.2 <0.3.0-0` covers the whole 0.2.1 series without touching it every rc; `0.2.1-rc.2 || 0.2.1-rc.3` breaks the day the next rc ships. Full walkthrough in [docs/article-engine-incompatible.md](docs/article-engine-incompatible.md).
2. **The compatibility field belongs to the host, and keys get namespaced.** The core stores `requirements['<host-id>/<requirement-name>']`, mapped by `requirementKeyOf` (DSH's `engines.dsh` → `dsh/dsh`) and stripped again on write-back. Do not expect raw host field names in the core.
3. **Declare resources by kind.** The unified kinds are `command` / `tool` / `skill` / `model` / `prompt` / `config` / `file` / `ui-slot` / `transport`. One resource collapses into different structures per host (a UI slot becomes `sidebar.panellist` + `main` in DSH); that mapping is `HostAdapter.resources.map`, and a resource the host cannot carry returns `null` rather than pretending to work.
section: For plugin authors: manifests and resource mapping

text:
plugbox README · Compatibility and limits：- Verified against DeepSeek Harness `0.2.1-rc.5` (npm `latest`). After a host upgrade, run `npm run check:engines` to re-check the index.
- Compatibility is decided host-side: when `engines.dsh` exists it is the only criterion (peer dependencies are ignored), evaluated as `semver.satisfies(runtime, range, { includePrerelease: true })`. That rule belongs to the DSH ecosystem and is implemented by the DSH adapter's `satisfies`; if an adapter does not implement it, the core returns `unknown` instead of guessing.
- Branch installs show the declared range but cannot predict compatibility: the runtime version is not exposed to the page, and the decision happens at install time.
- One published version per plugin in the index. Other versions are reachable through branch installs or by bumping the index.
- No plugin configuration UI: the DSH remote surface exposes bundle/row enablement plus install and remove only. Configuration schemas live on the model side (`Config.listConfigs`).
- Unverified adapters are never selected as the default host adapter.

plugbox README · FAQ：**How is this different from the host's built-in Discover page?**
Both read the same host services. Discover browses one index at a time; PlugBox merges sources and adds author facets, compatibility flags and branch installs.

plugbox README · FAQ：**Which hosts does PlugBox support?**
See the support matrix above. Only DeepSeek Harness is currently verified on a real host; the DeepSeek Harness shipped by zcode is a known host but not yet verified. Adding a host means one adapter plus a little configuration — no core changes.

plugbox README · FAQ：**Is "PlugBox catalog" the same as host official?**
No. It only means the plugin is listed in this repository's index. Host-official entries are decided by each host's own marker (for DSH, `official` in the entry's `labels`), and the two are shown as different badges.

plugbox README · FAQ：**Why does a plugin say "version mismatch"?**
That version's declared compatibility range (`engines.dsh`) does not include your DSH version. The card shows the required range; upgrade DSH or wait for the plugin to widen it. See [docs/article-engine-incompatible.md](docs/article-engine-incompatible.md) for the full walkthrough.

plugbox README · FAQ：**How is a branch install different from a normal install?**
A normal install uses the commit recorded in the index. A branch install uses the branch's current head commit, which moves with upstream pushes — meant for unreleased fixes.

**Why restart after installing?**
Host-side plugin code loads when DSH starts. Frontend assets can hot-update; host code cannot.

plugbox README · FAQ：**The index is subscribed but nothing shows up?**
Check the URL in a browser (it should return JSON), then click **Check for updates** to refresh the cache. jsDelivr caches for ~12 hours; use the purge command above if needed.

plugbox README · FAQ：**Do the old DeepSeekBox subscribe URLs still work?**
No. The repository has been renamed to **Wcof/PlugBox** and the old `Wcof/DeepSeekBox` index URLs are dead. Remove the old entries under *Index sources* and subscribe to `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Wcof/PlugBox/main/index.json` (or its jsDelivr counterpart) instead; an already installed old copy can be replaced by installing again from the new URL using option 2.

plugbox README · Development：```bash
npm install
npm run dev              # dev server at http://localhost:5180 with mocked host RPC
npm run build            # type check + build into web/, then postbuild (index sync and validations)
npm run preview          # preview the build output

Stack: Vue 3 `<script setup>` + TypeScript + Vite, no UI library and no router, hand-written CSS. `web/` is the committed build artifact — DSH does not run a build when installing from git, and a missing `web/` returns 503.

plugbox README · Layout：```
index.js              host half: /plugbox/ static route + /plugbox/api/rpc
client.js             client half: sidebar entry + iframe panel
cordis.patch.yml      bundle patch (DSH protocol) inserting the panel row
icons/plugbox.svg     icon shown in the host sidebar

plugbox README · Data flow：The page only talks to `src/services/pluginService.ts`, which turns each action into a canonical verb (`status`, `listBundles`, `listPlugins`, `setBundleEnabled`, `setPluginEnabled`, `removeBundle`, `installBundle`, `listIndexes`, `setIndexes`, `searchMarket`, `repoBranches`) and posts `{ method, params }` to `/plugbox/api/rpc`. The host half maps those verbs through the active adapter's `methods` table and forwards them to DSH's `pluginManager` / `pluginMarket`. `repoBranches` is the only method not backed by a host service — it reads repository branches.

plugbox README · Data flow：The endpoint accepts POST from the same origin only, with a 512 KiB body limit. Install and remove run pnpm and can take minutes.
